body.heading: Slow down, look closer
paragraphs: The naturalist's core skill is not knowledge but attention: walking slowly, stopping often, and looking at small things as if they matter. A single hedge can hold beetles, spiders' webs, three kinds of leaf and a bird with strong opinions.
You do not need countryside. Pavement weeds, park trees, pigeons and clouds all reward a closer look, and your own street will surprise you within a week.

body.heading: Keep a tiny field notebook
paragraphs: Carry a small notebook or a notes page and record what you notice: date, place, what you saw, one question it raises. Sketches count double; drawing forces the kind of looking that memory alone skips.
Names can come later, from a book, an app or a knowledgeable friend. Noticing comes first. A notebook of your own observations, however humble, is the beginning of real natural history.

takeaway: Walk slowly, look at small things, and write down what you notice.
